title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 14)
summary: NH continues Hagakure book two: the strayed warrior who retreats into art and comfort, the one-sided devotion of the retainer, why humans persist at things with no return, open-mindedness versus bias, ignoring critics, humility before better people, and emotional timing in speech. He relates them to training, including the idea that a bodybuilder should be like a lion, resting until it is time to hunt.
claims: Body and spirit must both be strong; retreating into a purely spiritual or intellectual life misunderstands the path
Great art and literature tell a story and inspire; modern art relies on shock and color and leaves him feeling nothing
A good book is like a friend that stays with you for life, and you should feel a bit sad closing it
Comfort is an upgrade to enjoy when present; if you can only sleep in perfect conditions you have pigeonholed yourself
At some point you must specialize; trying to be everything, like a half-baked intellectual warrior, leaves you nothing
Youth's spare time should go to discovering who you are, not social media or following groups, because peak productivity in your 20s-30s leaves little free time
He can barely remember having nothing to do; his rare leisure is rest that serves future work and prevents burnout
'I don't have time to train' is a lie for most people; once you develop a taste for hard work you need it in your life
He believes loyalty must go both ways, unlike the one-sided devotion Hagakure praises
Humans evolved to seek results, yet unlike animals we can keep doing something that returns nothing, such as loving a discipline we have no talent for
Work is the great equalizer: grinding beats talent over time, though a talented person who works just as hard stays ahead, so work harder
Recognize your bias: traditionalists love the old and progressives the new, and both are wrong; keep an open mind without sliding into relativism
Lifters stubbornly stick for years with methods that do not work; try new things at least once
Dedicated lifters do not attack other disciplines; convinced of their own path, they feel no need to convince others or feed negativity
Mockery is healthy and you should not take yourself too seriously; warrior talk is for your own spirit, others will see it in your actions
About eight of ten people he meets have better bodybuilding genetic potential than him, though few actualize it; recognizing better people protects your spirit from bitterness
Train like a lion: move normally and rest through the day, then focus all intensity into the training window
Emotional timing in speech comes from the heart and cannot be crafted or used to manipulate
